display.title: Getting to Meet the King: The Alter Rebbe and the Yishuvnik
display.summary_short: How we meet the King in Elul through every brachah, why Rosh Hashanah is the 'head' of the year, and the village Jew who learned in yechidus with the Alter Rebbe that the Rebbe needed no informer.
display.summary_long: Continuing the Alter Rebbe's parable of the King in the field during Elul, the storyteller asks what it means to actually meet the King. He explains yechidus, with the story of a top student of the Rebbe Rashab who was told, 'As well as you know yourself, I know you better.' In a yechidus with the Rebbe, a boy from England is asked whether he has met the King yet; the Rebbe explains that every brachah, 'Baruch Atah', speaks to Hashem face to face, so we must say brachos slowly and sincerely, never with 'fake money'. Rosh Hashanah is called the head of the year because, as the Mitteler Rebbe teaches, it directs every day of the year, so free moments should be filled with Tehillim, as the Frierdiker Rebbe once urged the yeshivah students. Finally, a melamed sent by the Alter Rebbe brings the village Jew he teaches to the Alter Rebbe for Rosh Hashanah. In yechidus the Alter Rebbe gently lists mistakes a Jew can make, and the man storms out, sure the melamed informed on him, until the Alter Rebbe explains that he named no one. Moved, the man does teshuvah, apologizes, and becomes a devoted Chassid.
display.lesson: Every brachah is a meeting with the King, so say it carefully; use Rosh Hashanah well, since it sets the tone for the whole year.
